newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes slide with WTI, no ANS offer.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes slide with WTI, no ANS offer.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices slid midday Monday in line with a WTI/Cushing market that fell on technical selling, traders said.
Differentials remained notional, with the main producer of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude declining to offer for March or April deliveries, saying they were still assessing the market.
Meanwhile, buyers bid $1.60 a barrel under spot April WTI, with none bidding for March barrels of ANS.
Buyers refused to pay $1.10 under WTI, noting that U.S. Gulf sour grades, lookalikes to ANS, traded at a heavy discount to WTI.
West Texas Sour/Midland was talked $2.65 under WTI in the spot market.
Outright prices for ANS were talked $19.85/20.05 a barrel, down 75 cents from late Friday.
One buyer said he considered splitting a full cargo of Oriente crude rather than buy ANS.
IPL Energy Inc, a major Canadian pipeline operator, said Monday they would not apportion crude oil shipments on their line from Hardisty, Alberta, to the mid-Western U.S..
West Coast refiners can run light Canadian crudes instead of ANS

Traders said Line 63 prices stood at postings plus $0.95 - $1.05, with the WTI-based market assessed at minus $1.95 to minus $1.85 under WTI. Buyers and sellers said supplies remain adequate for March.
Kern River heavy crude remained $14 53/14.73 a barrel, trader said, with rumors more volumes moved east on the All-American pipeline.
